title: Prefixcache sanity sweeper and ephemeral slab rewrite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After a recent production incident that manifested as sporadic model output regressions and elevated tail latency, our triage identified a small-but-impactful set of prefix cache failure modes: transient key corruption from concurrent inserts, non-deterministic eviction ordering under slab fragmentation, and a slow memory leak during high-throughput prefix churn. This ticket implements a defensive, low-risk remediation plan we call the 'sanity sweeper' plus an ephemeral slab rewrite to reduce fragmentation and enable safe on-the-fly compaction.
action_items: Implement 'sanity sweeper' background worker (v1): periodic scans that validate prefix->value checksums and tombstone consistency; mark suspect entries for fenced repair instead of returning bad values
Add lightweight per-entry checksum + version field to prefixcache metadata; include compatibility code path for existing entries (migration path via sweeper)
Introduce deterministic eviction ordering for ephemeral slabs: switch LRU buckets to time-cohort ordering to avoid race-induced reordering under heavy concurrent inserts
Build ephemeral slab rewrite tool: offline/online routine that copies live entries to fresh slabs while maintaining atomic swap semantics and a brief fenced period to avoid double-allocations
Expose runtime flag to disable prefixcache read-path in case of emergency (to force bypass and rely on model runtime), include metrics and alerting when set
Add guarded memlimit soft cap and adaptive throttle: when slab fragmentation exceeds threshold, slow down inserts and backpressure upstream clients
Create end-to-end integration test that simulates high-churn insert/evict workloads with randomized crash/restart to reproduce leak class
Add targeted telemetry: per-slab fragmentation ratio, per-prefix-version-mismatch counter, corruption-detected counter, sweeper-repairs count
Ship canary rollout to 10% of live traffic with automated rollback on increased 95/99th token latency or error rate
Document runbook steps for sweeper failures and slab rewrite, include escalation steps and safe flags
decisions: Opted for incremental deployment: add checksums and sweeper first (minimal perf hit) before enabling the ephemeral slab rewrite to avoid large blast radius
Use CRC32c for per-entry checksum (fast, hardware-accelerated on many hosts) rather than SHA1 to minimize CPU impact
Do not block existing reads during initial rollout; reads return values unless sweeper marks entry as suspect (fenced). Full fencing only enabled post-canary
Eviction ordering change chosen over rebuilding global allocator to reduce implementation time and risk

2026-03-04: Design review with SRE and Perf (Diego R., Leah O.); scope for 'sanity sweeper' agreed

2026-03-08: Canary harness and telemetry dashboards created (Grafana dashboard id: rp-runtime-prefixcache-41234)
2026-03-10: Begin 10% canary; monitoring in-flight; no regressions observed so far
notes: Trade-offs: checksums add ~0.6% p99 CPU under microbench; acceptable vs risk of silent corruption
Sweeper frequency tuned: default 30s window for high-load clusters, 5m for low-traffic to limit extra I/O
Migration: sweeper will opportunistically backfill checksum/version on read-path to avoid dedicated migration job
Ephemeral slab rewrite planned as opt-in initially; will require cross-team coordination with ops for node-level maintenance windows
